texts.firmware.font_rom.about: The shapes CGA, MDA and Hercules cards draw text with. It is the file %1 of 86Box's ROM set, which you supply. Without it the screen stays blank.
texts.firmware.machine_rom.about: A ROM of the %1. It is the file %2 of 86Box's ROM set, which you supply.
texts.firmware.video_rom.about: The ROM of the %1 video card. It is the file %2 of 86Box's ROM set, which you supply.
texts.setting.bios.about: Which BIOS the machine starts with, for a machine that offers more than one. 'auto' is the machine's usual one. A BIOS the machine does not offer is refused when the project loads, with the list of those it offers. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.clockstart.about: The date and time (UTC) on the machine's clock when it is switched on. It never comes from your computer. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cpu.about: The processor and its speed. 'auto' is the first one the machine takes. One the machine does not take is refused when the project loads, with the list of those it takes. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.floppya.about: The drive in bay A. It must fit the disks you give it: a 5.25" 360k drive cannot read a 1.2M disk. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.floppyb.about: The drive in bay B, or 'none'. It works the same way as drive A:. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.fpu.about: A maths coprocessor (FPU) beside the processor: an 8087 for an 8088, a 287 for a 286. 'none' is a machine sold without one. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.framespersecond.about: How much of the machine's time one frame is: 100 makes a frame 10 ms, as in PCem movies. It is part of the movie: the same inputs at another rate make another run.
texts.setting.joystick.about: What is plugged into the game port. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which PC this is: the motherboard, its BIOS chips and the processors it takes. It decides which ROM files the project asks you for. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.memorykb.about: The memory (RAM) in kilobytes. 0 is the most the machine takes on its motherboard: 640 KB on an XT-class machine with enough sockets. Each machine has its own smallest and largest size, and a size outside them is brought inside them. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.mouse.about: The mouse plugged into the machine. A serial mouse takes the first serial port (COM1). A PS/2 mouse needs a machine with a PS/2 port. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sound.about: The sound card, beside the PC speaker every machine has. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.video.about: The graphics card. CGA, MDA and Hercules draw text with the IBM character ROM; EGA and VGA have a BIOS of their own. Each needs its ROM file. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.floppy_a.help: Disk images for drive A:. The first is in the drive when the machine starts. The disks are read only: a program cannot write to them yet.
texts.slot.floppy_b.help: Disk images for drive B:. It works the same way as drive A:. The Floppy drive B: setting must not be none.
